Usage

Adaptive single-Gaussian background (the running mean) per frame → (T, H, W) (video).

Runs a single-Gaussian background (Wren's Pfinder) holding a mean mean and a variance var per pixel, and returns mean after each frame. The foreground test is (frame - mean)^2 > k^2 var. With selective=True (default), mean / var of pixels judged to be foreground are not updated, so slowly moving objects do not melt into the background. The update rules are mean += α diff, var += α (diff^2 - var), with a lower bound of 1e-4 on var.

• video: a (T, H, W) array or a list of 2-D frames. Integers are normalised to [0, 1] by their maximum, float is clipped. NaN/Inf raise ValueError.

• alpha: learning rate in [0, 1]. Default 0.02 (time constant about 50 frames).

• k: [0, 100]. Multiple of the standard deviation regarded as foreground. Default 2.5.

• var_init: [1e-9, 1]. Initial variance at the first frame (the square of [0, 1] intensity). If too small, every pixel becomes foreground from the 2nd frame on, and selective stops the update.

• selective: whether to stop updating foreground pixels. With False, all pixels are always updated.

• Return value: (T, H, W) float64. t = 0 is the first frame itself.

• Failure: ValueError (shape, dtype, each range).

The foreground mask of the same model is running_gaussian_foreground (paired with the same arguments it is consistent frame by frame).

The videostream op running_gaussian_background bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps alpha (default 0.02) and b sweeps k (default 2.5).
